LESSON: READING 14.4.1 EXTENSIVE READING: SHORT STORY (CLASS READER)

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 14
Topic 14.4: Reading 14.4.1 Extensive reading: Short story (Class Reader)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 14.4.1 Extensive reading: Short story (Class Reader), part of Strand 14 in Grade 8 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Where does a writer get what to write about? 2. How are stories related to what happens in real life?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify the ideas in the short story,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 14.4.1 Extensive reading: Short story (Class Reader) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. relate the ideas from the short story to real life experiences,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 14.4.1 Extensive reading: Short story (Class Reader) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. appreciate the value of short stories in reflecting social issues.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 14.4.1 Extensive reading: Short story (Class Reader) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify the ideas in the short story,

   Reading 14.4.1 Extensive reading: Short story (Class Reader) helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. relate the ideas from the short story to real life experiences,

   Reading 14.4.1 Extensive reading: Short story (Class Reader) helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. appreciate the value of short stories in reflecting social issues.

   Reading 14.4.1 Extensive reading: Short story (Class Reader) helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. read a short story and identify ideas it conveys,

2. discuss the events and characters in a short story and the issues the writer brings out through them,

3. work with peers to make connections between the ideas in the short story and their own experiences and those of the people they know,

4. dramatise and record sections of the short story that reflect real life experiences. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. read a short story and identify ideas it conveys,
2. discuss the events and characters in a short story and the issues the writer brings out through them,
3. work with peers to make connections between the ideas in the short story and their own experiences and those of the people they know,
4. dramatise and record sections of the short story that reflect real life experiences. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 14.4.1 Extensive reading: Short story (Class Reader) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Problem solving: It is inculcated as the learner makes connections between the short stories and their own experiences.

• Communication and collaboration: It is achieved as the learner works in pairs or groups to undertake different tasks.

Values:
Social justice: It is enhanced as all learners with varied abilities dramatise and record sections of the short story that reflect real

life experiences.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Social cohesion: It is promoted as the learner relates the text to real life experiences and makes informed decisions in their lives.

Links to other Learning Areas:
The examination of the short story as a genre is related to analysis of texts in Kiswahili.
